rubric.why: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation, not an established fact.
rubric.description: Identifies a hypothesis as a tentative or proposed explanation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a tentative or proposed explanation.

rubric.why: A scientific hypothesis must be capable of testing.
rubric.description: States that a hypothesis can be tested.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning that it can be tested.

modelAnswer: A hypothesis is a tentative explanation for observations or a problem.
It must be capable of being tested.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a hypothesis and a deduction.

rubric.why: A deduction is a conclusion or prediction derived logically from a hypothesis.
rubric.description: Defines deduction as a logical conclusion or prediction drawn from a hypothesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a deduction is a logical conclusion or prediction based on a hypothesis.

rubric.why: A theory is an explanation supported by substantial evidence.
rubric.description: Defines theory as a well-supported explanation based on evidence.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a theory as a well-supported explanation or one supported by observations and experiments.

modelAnswer: A deduction is a logical conclusion or specific prediction drawn from a hypothesis.
A theory is a well-supported explanation based on repeated observations and experiments.

items.followUp: State two reasons why classification is useful in biology.

rubric.why: Classification arranges organisms into groups based on their shared and differing features.
rubric.description: States that classification groups organisms according to similarities and differences.

rubric.why: Classification helps with identification and study and can reveal relationships among organisms.
rubric.description: States another aim, such as facilitating identification or study, or showing relationships.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one valid additional aim.

modelAnswer: Classification groups organisms according to their similarities and differences.
It makes organisms easier to identify and study and helps show relationships among them.
